subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should Gateway operator scopes become an input to agent tool-policy resolution, and where should the new scope-aware policy contract live?
rationale: This would define a new authorization boundary across Gateway auth, agent tool filtering, config precedence, and multi-user trust semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the security guarantee or default behavior.

options.title: Design scope-aware tool policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract, enforcement layer, precedence rules, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Use existing session and sender primitives
options.body: Route the need through `toolsBySender`, session envelopes, binding policy, conversation identity modes, or tenant RBAC instead of adding operator-scope-based config.

options.title: Decline scope-based RBAC
options.body: Document operator scopes as control-plane only and direct multi-user isolation to separate Gateways or a broader tenant model.

recommendation.title: Design scope-aware tool policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers approve a typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent contract, enforcement layer, precedence rules, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across scoped conversation profiles, trust-model documentation, and sender-policy hardening adjacent to this boundary.
